title: fix: leaner CI, safer sweeps and team build guards
headline: CI sizes its runs from measured times within a 3 minute merge path; sweep approval reads the right worktree and commit; and the team build holds its own steps in code, from the test list to a ticket for each test added after the sweep.
alignment: v1.51.2 is the patch after build 24 and 1.51.1. Its items are the CI rows CI-A to CI-D, K357, K360, K361, K362, K363, K364, K366, K368 and K369, each unit opened by a test-only commit. K359 shipped first as 1.51.1; this patch carries its two tests. K367 moves to 1.51.3.

upgrading: Run install user, then install project: the hooks `agent-model.cjs`, call-cap.cjs, edit-fence.cjs, handoff-gate.cjs and the new why-rule.cjs with holds.json, the kit tools closeout.mjs, warm.mjs, plan-check.mjs, checklist.mjs and flow-check.mjs, the sweep's approve.mjs, the team build skill and its brief templates, the CI templates and the testing rule change.
limits: A review spawn with no Plan: line is counted apart from planned ones, and a relative plan path is keyed from the folder the hook runs in. The holds.json tier is set per hold but read in each gate's own code. The commit-shape tool miscounts a double-quoted test name. Plain `--changed` without `--pick` still trusts a coverage map off HEAD. The why parse is line based, not a full tokenizer: a test call reached through an array or `.call`, or hidden by a deliberate slash after a word that may be a name, is not seen; it stops slips, not a determined workaround. The hand-back gate passes a hand-back when its own check crashes, which goes to the owner.
